Algebra I · Lesson 7.4

Finding the Equation of a Line

Solve this lesson →All lessons

A slope is a number computed from a line that is already drawn. It can also be known before any line is drawn. One point and a slope, or two points, are enough to write an equation whose graph is that line, and once that equation is written, arithmetic gives every other point of the line.

Problem
A line has slope 33 and passes through (2,5)(2,5). The point (8,y)(8,y) is on that same line, and the slope between any two points of a line is the same. Enter the value of yy.
Show a hint
  • The slope between (2,5)(2,5) and (8,y)(8,y) is y−58−28−2y−5​, and that has to come out to 33.
  • The denominator is 66, so the equation is y−56=36y−5​=3. Multiply both sides by 66.
Show the full solution
The slope between the two points is y−58−2=y−568−2y−5​=6y−5​, and that equals 33, so y−5=18y−5=18 and y=23y=23​. The slope formula from 7.3 is used the other way round here, with the slope known and one coordinate unknown.
Problem
A line has slope 44 and passes through (5,3)(5,3), and (x,y)(x,y) is any other point on it. The slope between those two points is 44, so y−3x−5=4x−5y−3​=4. Multiply both sides by x−5x−5, expand, and solve for yy. The result reads y=4x+cy=4x+c for one number cc. Enter cc.
Show a hint
  • Multiplying both sides by x−5x−5 leaves y−3=4(x−5)y−3=4(x−5), and the 44 multiplies both terms inside the parentheses.
  • Expanding gives y−3=4x−20y−3=4x−20. Now add 33 to both sides.
Show the full solution
Multiplying by x−5x−5 gives y−3=4(x−5)=4x−20y−3=4(x−5)=4x−20, and adding 33 to both sides gives y=4x−17y=4x−17, so c=−17c=−17​. Check at the given point, 4(5)−17=34(5)−17=3. The constant is not the 33 from the point, because the −20−20 from expanding is added to it.
Key idea
Point-slope form. Let (x1,y1)(x1​,y1​) be a known point of a line with slope mm, and let (x,y)(x,y) be any other point of that line. The slope between the two is mm, so y−y1x−x1=mx−x1​y−y1​​=m. Multiplying both sides by x−x1x−x1​ gives y−y1=m(x−x1),y−y1​=m(x−x1​), which is point-slope form. It is built from one point and one slope and nothing else. The multiplied equation is true at (x1,y1)(x1​,y1​) as well, where both sides are 00, even though the fraction it was cleared from is undefined there, so its solution points are the whole line.
Problem
A line has slope −4−4 and passes through (−3,8)(−3,8). Enter the yy-coordinate of the point on that line whose xx-coordinate is 55.
Show a hint
  • Write point-slope with (x1,y1)=(−3,8)(x1​,y1​)=(−3,8). Because x1x1​ is negative, the factor x−x1x−x1​ is x+3x+3 and not x−3x−3.
  • The line is y−8=−4(x+3)y−8=−4(x+3). At x=5x=5 the bracket is 88, so multiply that by −4−4 and then solve for yy.
Show the full solution
Point-slope with (x1,y1)=(−3,8)(x1​,y1​)=(−3,8) and m=−4m=−4 gives y−8=−4(x+3)y−8=−4(x+3), and at x=5x=5 the right side is −4(8)=−32−4(8)=−32, so y=8−32=−24y=8−32=−24​. With x1=−3x1​=−3 the factor x−x1x−x1​ is x+3x+3, and using x−3x−3 instead gives −4(2)=−8−4(2)=−8 and the wrong value 00.
Problem
A line has slope 2772​ and passes through (3,5)(3,5). Enter the yy-coordinate of the point on that line whose xx-coordinate is 88. It is not a whole number, so enter it as a fraction in lowest terms.
Show a hint
  • The run from x=3x=3 to x=8x=8 is 55, and the rise is the slope times the run.
  • The rise is 27(5)=10772​(5)=710​. Write 55 as 357735​ before adding.
Show the full solution
The run is 8−3=58−3=5 and the rise is 27(5)=10772​(5)=710​, so y=5+107=357+107=457y=5+710​=735​+710​=745​​. A fractional slope is not a special case. It only means most runs give a yy that is not a whole number.
Key idea
Substituting the point and the slope. Putting mm, x1x1​ and y1y1​ into y−y1=m(x−x1)y−y1​=m(x−x1​) leaves xx and yy as the only letters, and that is already an equation of the line. Expanding is a separate step. The right side is mm times a difference, so expanding it gives y−y1=mx−mx1y−y1​=mx−mx1​, and adding y1y1​ to both sides gives y=mx−mx1+y1y=mx−mx1​+y1​, the line solved for yy. The number added to mxmx is y1−mx1y1​−mx1​ and not y1y1​. Both equations have the same solution points, so both are equations of the same line.

Point-slope form is built from a point and a slope, and two points of a line give both. Either of the two is the point, and mm is the slope computed from the pair. So two points are enough to write the equation of the line through them, and the next two problems do exactly that.

Problem
A line passes through (1,10)(1,10) and (6,−5)(6,−5). Enter the yy-coordinate of the point on that line whose xx-coordinate is 88.
Show a hint
  • The slope is not stated here. Compute it from (1,10)(1,10) and (6,−5)(6,−5) first, then use point-slope form with either of those points.
  • The slope is −5−106−1=−36−1−5−10​=−3. Now work from (6,−5)(6,−5) with a run of 22.
Show the full solution
The slope is −5−106−1=−155=−36−1−5−10​=5−15​=−3. From (6,−5)(6,−5), the run out to x=8x=8 is 22 and the rise is −3(2)=−6−3(2)=−6, so y=−5−6=−11y=−5−6=−11​. Reversing only one of the two differences gives +3+3 for the slope, and the answer then comes out 11 instead.
Problem
A line passes through (−4,3)(−4,3) and (8,11)(8,11). Exactly one point of that line has yy-coordinate 1515. Enter that point's xx-coordinate.
Show a hint
  • The number given here is a yy-coordinate, so the unknown is xx. Start with the slope of the two given points.
  • The slope is 11−38−(−4)=238−(−4)11−3​=32​, so 15−11=23(x−8)15−11=32​(x−8).
Show the full solution
The slope is 11−38−(−4)=812=238−(−4)11−3​=128​=32​. Using (8,11)(8,11), 15−11=23(x−8)15−11=32​(x−8), so 4=23(x−8)4=32​(x−8), then x−8=6x−8=6 and x=14x=14​. Checking with (−4,3)(−4,3), 15−314−(−4)=1218=2314−(−4)15−3​=1812​=32​, the same slope. A slope of 2332​ does not force a fractional answer, since the run 32⋅423​⋅4 is whole.
Key idea
From two points, compute the slope first. Given two points (x1,y1)(x1​,y1​) and (x2,y2)(x2​,y2​) with different xx-coordinates, compute m=y2−y1x2−x1m=x2​−x1​y2​−y1​​, then substitute that mm and either of the two points into y−y1=m(x−x1)y−y1​=m(x−x1​). The order is forced, since point-slope form contains mm and no substitution is possible until mm is a number. Subtract in the same order top and bottom, taking the same point first in both. Mixing the two orders leaves mm with the wrong sign, and unless m=0m=0 the result is an equation of a different line.

There are two choices for (x1,y1)(x1​,y1​), one for each of the two points, and every problem so far used only one of them. Choosing the other point puts different numbers into point-slope form, so the two equations do not look alike until one of them is expanded. The next problem rebuilds an earlier line from its other point.

Problem
The line through (1,10)(1,10) and (6,−5)(6,−5) has slope −3−3. Substitute the point (6,−5)(6,−5) and that slope into point-slope form, expand, and solve for yy. The result reads y=−3x+cy=−3x+c. Enter cc.
Show a hint
  • With (x1,y1)=(6,−5)(x1​,y1​)=(6,−5), the left side is y−(−5)y−(−5), which is y+5y+5.
  • The equation is y+5=−3(x−6)y+5=−3(x−6). Expand the right side before moving the 55.
Show the full solution
Substituting gives y−(−5)=−3(x−6)y−(−5)=−3(x−6), which is y+5=−3x+18y+5=−3x+18, so y=−3x+13y=−3x+13 and c=13c=13​. Starting from (1,10)(1,10) instead gives y−10=−3(x−1)y−10=−3(x−1), and that expands to y=−3x+13y=−3x+13 as well. The two point-slope equations look different and describe the same line.
Fun fact
In the 1760s Johann Heinrich Lambert drew a straight line through measurements that did not all lie on one, then read values off that line at points he had never measured and used those readings as data.
Problem
A line passes through (−6,−2)(−6,−2) and (4,3)(4,3). Enter the yy-coordinate of the point on that line whose xx-coordinate is 1515, as a fraction in lowest terms.
Show a hint
  • Take (−6,−2)(−6,−2) first in both differences of the slope. Both involve subtracting a negative number, so write them out before simplifying.
  • The slope is 3−(−2)4−(−6)=124−(−6)3−(−2)​=21​, so point-slope from (4,3)(4,3) gives y−3=12(x−4)y−3=21​(x−4). Put x=15x=15 into that.
Show the full solution
The slope is 3−(−2)4−(−6)=510=124−(−6)3−(−2)​=105​=21​, so point-slope from (4,3)(4,3) gives y−3=12(x−4)y−3=21​(x−4). At x=15x=15 that reads y−3=12(11)=112y−3=21​(11)=211​, so y=172y=217​​. The xx asked for sits to the right of both given points, and the work is no different from finding yy at an xx between them.
Key idea
Either point gives the same line. From (1,10)(1,10) the equation is y−10=−3(x−1)y−10=−3(x−1), from (6,−5)(6,−5) it is y+5=−3(x−6)y+5=−3(x−6), and expanding either one gives y=−3x+13y=−3x+13. That holds in general. Subtracting y−y2=m(x−x2)y−y2​=m(x−x2​) from y−y1=m(x−x1)y−y1​=m(x−x1​) leaves y2−y1=m(x2−x1)y2​−y1​=m(x2​−x1​), which is the slope formula with the denominator cleared. It contains no xx and no yy, so it is true at every point, and the two equations have the same solution points. Either point is a valid choice, so take the one with the easier arithmetic.

Every pair of points so far had two different xx-coordinates. When the two xx-coordinates are equal, x2−x1x2​−x1​ is 00, the quotient is a division by zero, and the line has no slope at all. Point-slope form contains mm, so with no slope there is nothing to substitute into it. The next problem is that case.

Problem
A line passes through (−5,11)(−5,11) and (−5,−6)(−5,−6). One point on that line has yy-coordinate 6060. Enter that point's xx-coordinate.
Show a hint
  • Start with the slope through the two given points, and look hard at the denominator x2−x1x2​−x1​ before dividing.
  • There is no slope, so point-slope form cannot be used here at all. Compare the two first coordinates, then recall the vertical lines from 7.2.
Show the full solution
Both given points have first coordinate −5−5, so this is the vertical line x=−5x=−5, and the point with yy-coordinate 6060 is (−5,60)(−5,60), whose xx-coordinate is −5−5​. The slope −6−11−5−(−5)−5−(−5)−6−11​ has denominator 00, so this line has no slope and point-slope form does not apply. The second coordinate is unrestricted here, so the 6060 is not needed.
Problem
The points (−4,9)(−4,9), (2,−3)(2,−3) and (k,−13)(k,−13) all lie on one straight line. Enter kk.
Show a hint
  • Two of the three points are fully known, and two points are enough to pin the line. Start there.
  • Find the slope from the two known points, then put that slope and (2,−3)(2,−3) into point-slope form and substitute x=kx=k and y=−13y=−13.
Show the full solution
The first two points give slope −3−92−(−4)=−126=−22−(−4)−3−9​=6−12​=−2, and from (2,−3)(2,−3), −13−(−3)=−2(k−2)−13−(−3)=−2(k−2), so −10=−2(k−2)−10=−2(k−2), then k−2=5k−2=5 and k=7k=7​. The line is y=−2x+1y=−2x+1, and −2(7)+1=−13−2(7)+1=−13 checks it. Three points lie on one line exactly when the third satisfies the equation of the line through the other two.
Key idea
Two points with the same xx-coordinate give x=kx=k. If (k,y1)(k,y1​) and (k,y2)(k,y2​) are two different points of a line, the slope formula has 00 underneath, so the line has no slope and point-slope form does not apply. Every point of that line has first coordinate kk, with no condition on the second, so its equation is x=kx=k, the vertical line of 7.2. Two points with the same yy-coordinate are the opposite case. There the slope is 00, which is an ordinary number, so point-slope form does apply and gives y−y1=0y−y1​=0, which is y=y1y=y1​.

A quantity that changes at a constant rate has a straight line for its graph, and the rate is the slope of that line. Two readings of the quantity are two points of that line, so two readings are enough to determine the whole relationship, including its value at a moment nobody measured.

Problem
A machine winds cable onto a drum at a constant rate. Three minutes after the machine starts, the drum holds 5252 metres of cable, and ten minutes after it starts, the drum holds 115115 metres. The drum was not empty when the machine started. Enter how many metres of cable the drum held at the moment the machine started.
Show a hint
  • Time and length are the two coordinates. The readings are the points (3,52)(3,52) and (10,115)(10,115), and the constant rate is the slope.
  • The rate is 115−5210−3=910−3115−52​=9 metres per minute, so step back 33 minutes from the first reading.
Show the full solution
The readings are the points (3,52)(3,52) and (10,115)(10,115), so the rate is 115−5210−3=637=910−3115−52​=763​=9 metres per minute. Stepping back 33 minutes from (3,52)(3,52) gives 52−9(3)=2552−9(3)=25​. Dividing 115115 by 1010 gives 11.511.5, which is the rate only for a drum that starts empty.
Problem
A line passes through (−2,11)(−2,11) and (6,−5)(6,−5). Exactly one point of that line has its yy-coordinate equal to three times its xx-coordinate. Enter that point's xx-coordinate, as a fraction in lowest terms.
Show a hint
  • Find the equation of the line first. The stated condition describes one point of it and says nothing extra about the line.
  • The line is y=−2x+7y=−2x+7. A point on it whose yy-coordinate is three times its xx-coordinate satisfies 3x=−2x+73x=−2x+7.
Show the full solution
The slope is −5−116−(−2)=−168=−26−(−2)−5−11​=8−16​=−2, and from (−2,11)(−2,11), y−11=−2(x+2)y−11=−2(x+2), so y=−2x+7y=−2x+7. The condition is y=3xy=3x, so 3x=−2x+73x=−2x+7, then 5x=75x=7 and x=75x=57​​. The point is (75,215)(57​,521​), and −2(75)+7=215−2(57​)+7=521​ confirms it.

Nearly every line here came from a point and a slope, and each of those equations was left in point-slope form or solved for yy. The exception was the vertical line, which has no slope, so it is written x=kx=k instead. Lesson 7.5, Intercepts and Standard Forms, gives the two standard ways of writing a line and reads the slope straight off each one.

Practice these ideas

Practice
A line has slope 55 and passes through (1,2)(1,2). Enter the yy-coordinate of the point on that line whose xx-coordinate is 33.
Show the solution
The run is 3−1=23−1=2 and the rise is 5(2)=105(2)=10, so y=2+10=12y=2+10=12​.
Practice
A line has slope 33 and passes through (−1,4)(−1,4). Enter the yy-coordinate of the point on that line whose xx-coordinate is 55.
Show the solution
Point-slope gives y−4=3(x−(−1))y−4=3(x−(−1)), and at x=5x=5 the right side is 3(6)=183(6)=18, so y=22y=22​. Checking, the slope from (−1,4)(−1,4) to (5,22)(5,22) is 186=3618​=3.
Practice
A line has slope −4−4 and passes through (6,2)(6,2). Enter the yy-coordinate of the point on that line whose xx-coordinate is 99.
Show the solution
Point-slope with m=−4m=−4 and (6,2)(6,2) gives y−2=−4(x−6)y−2=−4(x−6). At x=9x=9 that reads y−2=−4(3)=−12y−2=−4(3)=−12, so y=−10y=−10​. The slope is negative, so the point three to the right of (6,2)(6,2) lies below it rather than above.
Practice
A line has slope 55 and passes through (4,−3)(4,−3). Solved for yy, its equation reads y=5x+cy=5x+c. Enter cc.
Show the solution
Point-slope form gives y+3=5(x−4)=5x−20y+3=5(x−4)=5x−20, so y=5x−23y=5x−23 and c=−23c=−23​. Reading cc off y+3=5x−20y+3=5x−20 gives −20−20, which skips the last subtraction. Checking, 5(4)−23=−35(4)−23=−3.
Practice
A line has slope 3553​ and passes through (5,1)(5,1). Enter the yy-coordinate of the point on that line whose xx-coordinate is 99, as a fraction in lowest terms.
Show the solution
The run is 44 and the rise is 35(4)=12553​(4)=512​, so y=1+125=55+125=175y=1+512​=55​+512​=517​​.
Practice
A line has slope 44 and passes through (3,−1)(3,−1). Enter the xx-coordinate of the point on that line whose yy-coordinate is 1919.
Show the solution
From (3,−1)(3,−1) with slope 44, 19−(−1)=4(x−3)19−(−1)=4(x−3), so 20=4(x−3)20=4(x−3), then x−3=5x−3=5 and x=8x=8​.
Practice
A line passes through (2,1)(2,1) and (5,10)(5,10). Enter the yy-coordinate of the point on that line whose xx-coordinate is 88.
Show the solution
The slope is 10−15−2=35−210−1​=3, so the line through (5,10)(5,10) is y−10=3(x−5)y−10=3(x−5). At x=8x=8, y−10=3⋅3=9y−10=3⋅3=9, so y=19y=19​. Using (2,1)(2,1) instead gives y−1=3(x−2)y−1=3(x−2) and the same 1919 at x=8x=8.
Practice
A line passes through (−3,8)(−3,8) and (1,0)(1,0). Enter the yy-coordinate of the point on that line whose xx-coordinate is 44.
Show the solution
The slope is 0−81−(−3)=−84=−21−(−3)0−8​=4−8​=−2. From (1,0)(1,0) the run out to x=4x=4 is 33, so the rise is 3⋅(−2)=−63⋅(−2)=−6 and y=0−6=−6y=0−6=−6​. Measuring the run from x=0x=0 instead of from x=1x=1 gives a run of 44 and the wrong value −8−8.
Practice
A line passes through (−1,−2)(−1,−2) and (3,10)(3,10). Enter the xx-coordinate of the point on that line whose yy-coordinate is 2828.
Show the solution
The slope is 10−(−2)3−(−1)=124=33−(−1)10−(−2)​=412​=3. From (3,10)(3,10), 28−10=3(x−3)28−10=3(x−3), so 18=3(x−3)18=3(x−3), then x−3=6x−3=6 and x=9x=9​.
Practice
A line passes through (−4,3)(−4,3) and (−4,11)(−4,11). Enter the xx-coordinate of the point on that line whose yy-coordinate is −60−60.
Show the solution
Both given points have first coordinate −4−4, so the change in xx is 00 and there is no slope. The line is x=−4x=−4, so every point on it has x=−4x=−4​. There is no slope to substitute into point-slope form, so it does not apply here, and the −60−60 is not needed.
Practice
A line passes through (−7,5)(−7,5) and (4,5)(4,5). Solved for yy, its equation reads y=ax+by=ax+b for two numbers aa and bb. Enter aa.
Show the solution
The change in yy is 5−5=05−5=0 and the change in xx is 4−(−7)=114−(−7)=11, so the slope is 011=0110​=0 and the coefficient of xx is 00​. The line is horizontal, and every point on it has y=5y=5 whatever xx is.
Practice
The line through (1,5)(1,5) and (4,17)(4,17) also passes through (9,k)(9,k). Enter kk.
Show the solution
The slope is 17−54−1=44−117−5​=4, so point-slope from (1,5)(1,5) gives y−5=4(x−1)y−5=4(x−1). At x=9x=9, k=5+4(8)=37k=5+4(8)=37​.
Practice
A line passes through (−3,2)(−3,2) and (7,10)(7,10). Enter the yy-coordinate of the point on that line whose xx-coordinate is 44, as a fraction in lowest terms.
Show the solution
The slope is 10−27−(−3)=810=457−(−3)10−2​=108​=54​, so the line is y−2=45(x+3)y−2=54​(x+3). At x=4x=4 that reads y−2=45(7)=285y−2=54​(7)=528​, so y=385y=538​​.
Practice
A line passes through (−6,14)(−6,14) and (2,−2)(2,−2). Solve for yy to write its equation as y=mx+cy=mx+c for two numbers mm and cc. Enter cc.
Show the solution
The slope is −2−142−(−6)=−168=−22−(−6)−2−14​=8−16​=−2. From (2,−2)(2,−2), y+2=−2(x−2)=−2x+4y+2=−2(x−2)=−2x+4, so y=−2x+2y=−2x+2 and c=2c=2​. From (−6,14)(−6,14), y−14=−2(x+6)=−2x−12y−14=−2(x+6)=−2x−12 gives y=−2x+2y=−2x+2 as well.
Practice
A candle burns down at a constant rate. It stands 2121 cm tall 1212 minutes after it is lit and 1616 cm tall 3232 minutes after it is lit. Enter its height in centimeters at the moment it was lit.
Show the solution
The rate is 16−2132−12=−520=−1432−1216−21​=20−5​=−41​ cm per minute. Over the 1212 minutes before the first reading the candle lost 33 cm, so its height at the moment it was lit is 2424​. Checking, 24−14⋅32=1624−41​⋅32=16, which matches the second reading.
Practice
A tank drains at a constant rate, and time is measured in minutes from the moment it starts draining. At 33 minutes it holds 9292 liters and at 1111 minutes it holds 6868 liters. Enter the number of minutes at which it holds 5050 liters.
Show the solution
The rate is 68−9211−3=−248=−311−368−92​=8−24​=−3 liters per minute. From (3,92)(3,92), 50−92=−3(t−3)50−92=−3(t−3), so −42=−3(t−3)−42=−3(t−3), then t−3=14t−3=14 and t=17t=17​.
Practice
A line passes through (−6,13)(−6,13) and (−6,−2)(−6,−2), and the point (4k,40)(4k,40) is on that same line. Enter kk.
Show the solution
Both given points have first coordinate −6−6, so the line has no slope and its equation is x=−6x=−6. A point is on it exactly when its first coordinate is −6−6, so 4k=−64k=−6 and k=−32k=−23​​. The 4040 is not needed, since x=−6x=−6 is true for every value of yy.
